chunks: And from him, from Bakr ibn Salih, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that I had refrained from seeking children for five years, and that was because my wife disliked it and said: 'Their upbringing is difficult for me due to the scarcity of means. So what is your opinion?'
So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: 'Seek children, for God, Mighty and Majestic, will provide for them.'

key_terms.اجْتَنَبْتُ طَلَبَ الْوَلَدِ: refraining from seeking children — deliberately avoiding procreation
key_terms.اطْلُبِ الْوَلَدَ: seek children — an imperative command to procreate
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — honorific for God emphasizing His power and authority
key_terms.لِقِلَّةِ الشَّيْءِ: due to the scarcity of means — fear of poverty as an excuse
key_terms.يَرْزُقُهُمْ: will provide for them — divine providence covers children's sustenance

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to avoid having children due to financial hardship?
ai.summary: Bakr ibn Salih consulted Imam Abu al-Hasan (AS) about his and his wife's decision to avoid having more children due to financial hardship. The Imam instructed him to seek children regardless, grounding the ruling in theological certainty: God is the ultimate provider and children's sustenance is His responsibility. This hadith establishes the Islamic teaching that fear of poverty is not a valid reason to abstain from procreation.
